claim.short: The 11-pathway translation/proteostasis signature first observed as the driver of mouse-gastrocnemius -> human-Inspiration4-skin transfer (PR #8) reproduces across every other Inspiration4 PBMC subset (B, CD4_T, CD8_T, CD14_Mono, CD16_Mono, DC, NK, other_T, other) and across all NASA_Twins CD4 / CD8 PolyA+/Ribodepleted/Multivariate contrasts. 23 of 25 valid human compartments show mean proteostasis-11 NES below -2.0; the mouse gastrocnemius anchor mean is -2.25, matching the human PBMC range. The 14 non-proteostasis pathways from the same 25-pathway overlap show a weaker, less uniform suppression pattern across compartments, supporting that ribosomal-protein-driven translation suppression is the specifically conserved cross-tissue spaceflight signal rather than a generic 'everything goes down' effect.

metrics.name: n_compartments_proteostasis11_perm_p_lt_005
metrics.context: Most compartments are Twins with n=4 pathways; only i4_skin (n=11) reaches significance.

validation.notes: Per-compartment Spearman r against the mouse gastrocnemius NES vector is noisy because NASA_Twins compartments only have n=4 of the 11 proteostasis pathways present (Twins covers C2/Hallmark, not C5). The conclusion is therefore anchored on the per-compartment mean NES distribution (23/25 below -2.0 for proteostasis_11), not on per-compartment Spearman significance. HPC c2cgp/c5bp expansion will raise the per-compartment overlap and let the Spearman side reach significance more broadly.
